inventedEvidence.evidence: Calls it 'your Panasonic NNH98 microwave' after the customer stated the model is NN-CD87KSBPQ - a contradiction rather than an invented check

confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'Overheat cut-out or control' heading is misdirected but hedged with 'often due to'

rationale: The assistant never interpreted H98 (no microwave output - magnetron/inverter) despite the customer explicitly clarifying it was a display code and giving the full model NN-CD87KSBPQ; it kept calling the appliance a 'Panasonic NNH98', asked whether it was in grill mode after being told grill works, and offered an unsupported 'overheat cut-out' direction and a vent check. Safety was handled well (do not open the casing, HV warning) and it did refer to an engineer, but it ignored the 'is it worth fixing' question and gave no useful context about the likely fault, so the homeowner leaves with a correct hand-off but little understanding.
